svg.text: One tool-calling loop with five tools and a bounded number of steps.
The same loop with its limits, schemas and failure handling; what changed is outlined in amber.
system prompt: what the page blocks are,
which tool for what, rules on honesty
+ the chat history, page blocks in each user message
reads the input, calls tools, reads the results,
repeats until it writes its answer
prices and dates only from tool results
a failed tool returns an error to the agent,
which tells the user instead of guessing
agent errors are recorded in the chat history
forms the new request (keep, change, drop) and runs the
search function in the same step (choice G)
trips on screen + a date window: bookable departures,
and the nearest ones outside the window (choice K)
the day-by-day plan of a trip
in-house RAG: general articles + the destination’s (choice L)
asks “connect to a human agent?”; Yes freezes the chat
Routing: a rule in the system prompt
asks WHEN, for the trips on screen
asks for a person, or no tool can answer
• One loop, with the rules in the tools; the agent decides what to keep, change or drop (choices G, J).
• It asks nothing the page already answers: the page state is in each user message (choice E).
• Undo is not a tool; asked to go back, the agent forms the earlier request with search_trips.
• Hand-over: when it can’t answer, the chat asks; Yes freezes the chat (next step B).
• During a turn the controls are locked and stop cancels the turn (choice N).
shape checked; must end with a user message
system prompt + history; the page blocks come
model: claude-haiku-5-5, reasoning at its default
every tool is guarded: a throw gives the agent
only “<tool> failed: not available right now”
usage is counted, never sent to the client
the answer = text of the last non-empty step
a promised connection is replaced in code by
“I can offer you a human agent.”
the page is never involved; no detail leaks
in: { tripIds?, from?, to? } · out: DeparturesResult
trips on screen only; says how many it checked
returns articles; the agent judges whether they cover
in: {} · out: a string · ends the turn
the question’s text is written by code
Routing: a rule in the system prompt
asks WHEN, for the trips on screen
asks for a person, or no tool can answer
What changed while building, and what was measured
• hand_over ends the turn (6 of 14 turns had failed on an empty final step); the answer is the last non-empty text.
• A promised connection (3 of 3 live runs) is replaced in code, with a test; stale trips are not priced (issue 12).
• Tools answer for the trips on screen; the FAQ tool can’t judge coverage, the agent does (issue 18).
• A turn costs 2–5 hundredths of a cent in 1–3 s. Live eval: 22 cases, 3 runs, 69 turns, 64 clean (67 after a check fix).
• Measured and kept: reasoning at the default (lower broke the tools in 2 turns).
Left: the plan (DESIGN.md) · Right: the prototype as built (BUILD.md)
